history.recommendation_text: The Board also recommended that the Administration support improvements in the process of developing joint workplans for the countries that signed United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks and form joint steering committees that become operational.
history.administration_response: The inter-agency working group on programme development and results endorsed the technical tip sheet on joint workplans in December 2021. The tip sheet was immediately disseminated through the policy bulletin to resident coordinators, United Nations country teams and United Nations Sustainable Development Group entities at the global level (and made available on the Group’s knowledge portal, accessible to all staff of those entities). In addition, tailored individual messages were sent to all resident coordinators of countries for which there was no joint workplan recorded in UN-Info (https://uninfo.org/). As a result, a number of countries implementing the Cooperation Framework and that have a joint workplan in place according to UN-Info has increased from 38 per cent to 90 per cent. The provision of tailored support to resident coordinators and country teams continues. In 2021, 76 per cent of Cooperation Framework countries have established a national-United Nations steering committee, up from 66 per cent in 2020. Therefore, the Development Coordination Office considers that the recommendation has been addressed and implemented and thus requests the Board to close this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that, as at 31 December 2021, of 42 countries implementing Cooperation Frameworks, 4 countries (12.5 percent) had not been entered into UN-Info and 38 countries had not completed the upload of the joint workplans to UN-Info, and that, 10 countries (32 per cent) had not established or fully established their joint steering committees, which meant that (a) there were no terms of reference; (b) terms of reference had been drafted but not endorsed by the country team and the Government; or (c) the steering committee was in place, with terms of reference, but it was not meeting on a regular basis, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration support improvements in the process of developing joint workplans for the countries that signed United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks and form joint steering committees that become operational.
history.administration_response: By the end of 2022, 87 per cent of countries implementing a United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework had developed a joint workplan in UN-Info, meaning that significant progress was achieved in terms of compliance. Of the other 13 per cent (16 countries), three United Nations country teams (Libya, Sao Tome and Principe and Mauritius) have joint workplans, but these were not yet public (the joint workplan for Libya was being prepared for publication; that of Sao Tome and Principe had not yet obtained a sign-off from its Government; and there were limitations in UN-Info with regard to the workplan for Mauritius). Ten United Nations country teams were in the process of developing their joint workplans as their new cycle had just started (Fiji, Samoa, the Federated States of Micronesia, the State of Palestine, Yemen and Myanmar), or because of past delays for reasons outside the country teams control (e.g. a delayed/outstanding Government signature on the Cooperation Framework (Saudi Arabia and Malaysia) or paused because of the impact of war (Eritrea and the Syrian Arab Republic)). For two country teams, joint workplans were not feasible (the United Arab Emirates has no Cooperation Framework, while in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, development work has been paused). Regarding joint steering committees, 90 per cent of countries with Cooperation Frameworks have established a joint steering committee, with 84 per cent meeting at least once in the last 12 months. This is an improvement of 14 per cent over 2021. Other countries are facing challenges of a political nature that have impeded the ability of joint steering committees to meet. Guidance and tracking support from the Development Coordination Office will not solve political issues at the country level. Based on the above, the Development Coordination Office requests that the Board close this recommendation, as the provision of support to improve the process has been achieved.
history.board_assessment: Given that the systematic backlogs of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework cycle have not yet been addressed, and further system-wide evaluation on Cooperation Frameworks is needed, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: By the end of 2022, 94 per cent of countries implementing a Cooperation Framework had developed a joint workplan on the UN-Info platform. This was significant progress in terms of compliance and a further improvement of 7 per cent compared with the end of 2021. All the remaining eight countries, or 6 per cent, had compelling reasons for not having a joint workplan, such as their multi-country nature or because they did not have an active Cooperation Framework. With regard to the joint steering committees, 90 per cent of Cooperation Framework countries have established a joint steering committee, with 84 per cent of these meeting at least once in the past 12 months. This is a 14 per cent improvement over 2021. The remaining countries are facing challenges of a political nature that have impeded the joint steering committee from meeting. The Administration considers the positive results mentioned as evidence that the recommendation has been implemented and therefore requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration support improvements in the process of developing joint workplans for the countries that signed United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks and form joint steering committees that become operational.
history.administration_response: By the end of 2023, all but two of the countries implementing a Cooperation Framework had developed a joint workplan in the UN-Info. The two United Nations country teams for which joint workplans are not feasible are the United Arab Emirates (which has no Cooperation Framework) and the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (where development work has been paused). Regarding the joint steering committees: 87 per cent (109 out of 125) of Cooperation Framework countries have established a joint national-United Nations steering committee, with 83 per cent of them meeting at least once in the last 12 months. Outstanding countries are facing challenges of political nature that have prevented the joint steering committee from meeting. Development Coordination Office guidance and tracking support will not solve political issues at the country level. Based on the above, the Development Coordination Office requests the Board to close this recommendation, as “support to improve the process” has been achieved.
history.board_assessment: Given that almost all countries implementing a Cooperation Framework had developed a joint workplan in UN-Info in 2023, and the majority of Cooperation Framework countries had established joint steering committees in 2023, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
